summary: Backend-only verification of the Admin DELETE /api/admin/users/{user_id} endpoint after frontend Alert.alert fix. Created /app/backend/tests/test_admin_delete_user.py with 5 pytest cases covering: admin login, unauthenticated rejection, non-existent user 404, self-delete 400, and full create->list->delete->verify-removed flow. All 5 tests pass against the preview URL (https://payment-flow-test-39.preview.emergentagent.com).
action_items: None for backend. The DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} endpoint works correctly end-to-end (auth, 404, self-delete protection, successful delete + DB cleanup + listing reflects removal). The original bug was purely the React Native Web Alert.alert callback issue, which is already fixed on the frontend (utils/alert.ts showConfirm). Main agent can self-verify the frontend fix in a real Expo web build.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~11,166 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Strongly recommend splitting by domain (auth, admin, bookings, payments, etc.) for maintainability.
Email validator in pydantic rejects the reserved TLD .test (RFC 6761). Not a bug, but worth knowing when seeding/test-fixturing — tests now use @example.com.

delete_user() correctly cascades deletions across users, user_sessions, bookings, tasks, messages, reviews. Consider also cleaning notifications, payment-related collections, and uploaded files if any, to avoid orphan rows.

success_rate.frontend: N/A (not in scope; Expo app not served in this pod)

seed_data_creation: Each run of test_create_then_delete_user_success registers a unique throwaway user (test_delete_<uuid>@example.com) and deletes it in the same test, leaving no residual data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable pytest module at /app/backend/tests/test_admin_delete_user.py covers admin user-deletion end-to-end. Run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_admin_delete_user.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/admin_delete_user.xml. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. Note: pydantic EmailStr rejects reserved TLDs like .test/.invalid/.localhost — always use @example.com for synthetic test emails.
rca_of_the_issue: Original reported bug (delete button not working) was a frontend React Native Web bug: Alert.alert button callbacks are no-ops on web, so the confirm dialog's onPress that would call DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} never fired. Backend was always healthy. Frontend fix replaced Alert.alert with a cross-platform showConfirm/showAlert in utils/alert.ts (already applied by main agent). This test suite confirms the backend side has no blocker: endpoint properly authenticates (401/403 without token), returns 404 on non-existent ids, returns 400 on self-delete, and on success returns 200 with a success message and removes the user from the database (verified via subsequent GET /api/admin/users and a re-DELETE returning 404).
